---
title: "Averaging error shares across reports"
subtitle: "2.19 · after the postrank theory book, chapters 8 and 22"
description: "Pooled errors, conditional mean error shares and zero-imputed means when disclosure varies."
---

When stated pair counts vary across reports or datasets, the average error share depends on whether we pool counts, average over disclosing outcomes only, or impute zero for silent reports.

```{=html}
<div id="app" class="prx-app column-page"></div>

<script src="../../js/bundles/averaging-errors.js"></script>
<script>window.__prxApp = PRX["averaging-errors"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("app"));</script>
```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Three outcomes.** Pooled pairs give 2/5, disclosing outcomes give 1/2, and zero-imputation gives 1/3 (disclosure chance 2/3, mean disclosure 5/9).
- **More weight on errors.** Increasing the error-heavy outcome's weight shifts the pooled ratio to 4/7, the disclosing mean to 2/3, and the zero-imputed mean to 1/2.
- **A complete-report lottery.** Mixing complete reports yields 1/8 for pooled expected counts versus 49/400 for the mean report fraction.
- **All silent.** Both ratio-based summaries read “NA: no disclosure,” while the zero-imputed mean is 0.
- **Twenty datasets.** Simulated league replays yield pooled error .0892 and disclosing mean .0891 against fixed true values.

<details>
<summary>Small-sample ratio note</summary>

A ratio estimated from a small sample need not be unbiased for a ratio of expectations. The hand-set outcomes provide an exact single-observation counterexample, while one trajectory of simulated datasets illustrates variability rather than repeated-sample bias.

</details>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In R"}
```r
A <- c(2, 0, 0); N <- c(2, 3, 0)
c(pooled=sum(A)/sum(N), disclosing=mean((A/N)[N>0]), zero_imputed=mean(ifelse(N>0,A/N,0)))
```
:::

Standalone: [averaging-errors](../../embed/averaging-errors.html), for example `?mode=replays&replays=5&cap=1`.
